correct_answer: Significant deficiency — the compensating control required by the SoD exception failed (no documented review within 5 business days), the review was not escalated to Audit Committee as required by POL-FIN-008 Section 4.6, and the invoice remains unmatched to the PO; the verbal Teams message cannot substitute for the required documented sign-off
rationale: This is a significant deficiency because multiple elements of the compensating control framework failed simultaneously. First, the 5-business-day review deadline (Dec 26) passed without documented Controller sign-off in the override log. Second, POL-FIN-008 Section 4.6(c) explicitly requires escalation to the Audit Committee when the review is not completed within 5 days — this escalation did not occur. Third, Wright's Teams DM to the auditor on Jan 8 confirms the review remains undocumented as of that date (13 business days late). A verbal statement in Teams that the transaction 'is legit' does not satisfy the documented sign-off requirement — the control is specifically designed to produce evidence. Additionally, the PO backfill was never linked, so the three-way match compensating control also remains incomplete. Answer B is wrong because a verbal confirmation in an informal DM is not 'documented review with sign-off' as the control requires — this conflates the substance (the transaction being legitimate) with the control evidence (the documented review). Answer B understates severity because it ignores the missed Audit Committee escalation and treats verbal confirmation as partially mitigating; the point of SOX controls is documented, auditable evidence. Answer D overstates because the override itself was properly authorized in advance (SA-2025-041 was approved by the CFO), the operational context is documented, and there is no indication of fraudulent intent — this is a compensating control timing failure, not a pervasive breakdown.
